P.text: A fee-on-transfer token is configured as the disputeToken, and a user calls disputeTree() with disputeAmount tokens, of which the contract receives fewer due to the transfer fee while recording the full disputeAmount.
P.evidence_quote: If a fee-on-transfer (FoT) token is configured as the `disputeToken`, the `resolveDispute()` function will permanently revert

I.text: resolveDispute() must be able to transfer back the recorded disputeAmount (in both branches) so the dispute can be cleared and disputer reset to address(0).
I.evidence_quote:
Both branches attempt to transfer `disputeAmount` (1000 tokens), but:
- Contract only holds 990 tokens

V.text: resolveDispute() always reverts because the contract holds fewer tokens than the recorded disputeAmount, leaving disputer non-zero permanently and bricking the protocol with no recovery path other than upgrade/migration.
V.evidence_quote:
Since `resolveDispute()` always reverts:
1. `disputer` remains set to the original disputer address (non-zero)
2. The dispute cannot be cleared through any mechanism
3. Protocol enters permanent freeze state
